title: The Effects of Environmental Shocks on the Treatment of Synthetic Pyridine-containing Wastewater by Aerobic Granular Sludge
description: Aerobic granular sludge (AGS) technology is effective for the treatment of toxic and refractory wastewater. However, the stability of AGS systems under environmental stress has not been sufficiently investigated. In this study, mature AGS was used to treat synthetic pyridine-containing wastewater at a pyridine concentration of 60 mg/L, and the effects of typical environmental shocks, including reactor shutdown, organic loading shock, loss of aeration-induced hydraulic shear force, reduction in the carbon-to-nitrogen (C/N) ratio, and shortened operating cycles, were evaluated in terms of the physicochemical properties of AGS, pollutant removal performance, and microbial community composition. The results showed that organic loading shock and loss of aeration-induced hydraulic shear force were the major factors affecting the stable operation of the AGS system. These stresses disrupted the balance among the components of extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), as indicated by a decreased protein-to-polysaccharide (PN/PS) ratio, which led to lower hydrophobicity and weaker mechanical strength and ultimately caused granule disintegration. Although environmental shocks did not significantly affect the removal of pyridine or chemical oxygen demand (COD), they markedly inhibited nitrogen removal. Compared with the stable operating phase, organic loading shock and loss of aeration-induced hydraulic shear force decreased the total nitrogen (TN) removal rate by 7.7% and 6.6%, respectively, and decreased the NH4+-N removal rate by 16.2% and 9.9%, respectively. High-throughput sequencing further revealed that organic loading shock and loss of aeration-induced hydraulic shear force reduced the abundance of EPS-producing bacteria and nitrogen-removing functional bacteria, which was closely associated with instability in granule structure and deterioration in nitrogen removal performance. This study clarifies the key effects of environmental shocks on the long-term stable operation of AGS under pyridine stress and provides a theoretical basis for the engineering application and operational regulation of AGS in the treatment of refractory nitrogen-containing heterocyclic wastewater.
